highlight.title: Gendered AI Risk: Women Face Amplified Labour Market Vulnerabilities as AI Transforms Workplaces
highlight.summary: A new arxiv study by Fernandez et al. (2026) conducts a gendered analysis of AI-driven workplace transformation, finding that existing structural inequalities in women's earnings and economic security risk amplification through AI adoption. The research identifies specific task and occupational categories where women face disproportionate displacement exposure. This has significant implications for modelling differential displacement rates across demographic groups in white-collar and professional roles.

highlight.title: Federal Reserve Publishes Framework for Tracking AI Buildout and Economic Impact Using Public Data
highlight.summary: A new FEDS Note by Soto, Thieu, and Allen presents a set of publicly available indicators organised into three categories to help researchers and policymakers track the generative AI buildout and its economic impact on a timely basis. The note is notable as an official Fed synthesis tool and signals growing institutional attention to real-time AI adoption measurement. This release partially addresses the overdue quarterly Fed AI adoption monitoring series last ingested in April 2026.

highlight.title: Yale Budget Lab Launches Ongoing AI Labor Market Tracker
highlight.summary: The Yale Budget Lab has published a dedicated tracker monitoring AI's impact on the US labour market, providing a regular institutional touchpoint for displacement and wage trend data. The tracker complements Yale's concurrent analysis of healthcare employment growth, underscoring the lab's focus on sectoral divergence in an AI-influenced economy. This is a high-value recurring data source for benchmarking overall US displacement trajectories.

highlight.title: Banking Sector AI Adoption Drives Contradictory Employment Outcomes, Literature Review Finds
highlight.summary: A systematic literature review by Chen (2026) in an open-access journal examines how widespread AI adoption in banking has produced simultaneous job displacement and new role creation, creating contradictory net labour market signals. The review draws on Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory frameworks alongside traditional labour economics to model worker behavioural responses to automation risk. Findings reinforce the difficulty of producing clean net displacement estimates for financial services without firm-level granularity.

highlight.title: Slovak Firm-Level Evidence Shows AI Adoption Stage Determines Whether Firms Hire or Cut — Net Figures Mislead
highlight.summary: Štetka, Hajduová, and Grisáková (2026) use firm-level survey data from Slovakia to demonstrate that aggregate employment figures mask simultaneous hiring and cutting occurring within the same firm during AI adoption, with the net effect highly contingent on adoption stage and self-assessed AI maturity. Early-stage adopters tend toward workforce expansion while mature adopters show consolidation and role elimination. The findings challenge single-figure displacement forecasts and call for stage-sensitive modelling of AI workforce reconfiguration.
